items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Roe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Roe provided Council with moments of reflection.

items.title: On June 6 we remembered Yumnah Afzaal, her mother Madia Salman,
notes: her grandmother Talat Afzaal and her father, Salman Afzaal, who were tragically killed 5 years ago while out for a walk in London, Ontario. We also remember their young brother, son and grandson who were seriously injured but survived. This painful anniversary is a reminder of the dangers of Islamophobia as well as the racism, hatred and violence that our Muslim neighbours continue to face.
As a City, we reaffirm our commitment to join with Muslim communities in the face of hate, and to challenge racism and discrimination in all its forms.

items.title: This past Friday we opened the month of celebrations for Indigenous
notes: History Month and Pride with our Beats in the Square community event.
Through music, dance, performances and community connection, we celebrated 2SLGBTQIA+ people and Indigenous history and identity.

Waterloo celebrates Pride and Indigenous History month with the belief that an inclusive city is one that recognizes differences and ensures residents have equal opportunities and benefits. We support an enhanced sense of belonging for all residents and a commitment to reconciliation.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Freeman informed Council that this past weekend, Saturday June 6, there was an assumption of command for the 31 Combat Engineer Regiment (the Elgin’s), which train in Waterloo and St. Thomas, for the new Commanding Officer Lieutenant- Colonel Adrian Dereniowski. It was a great change of command parade in St. Thomas, and the weather held out.

Councillor Hanmer gave a shoutout to staff for their work in the setup and delivery of the Pride and Indigenous History Month celebration in Waterloo Town Square on Friday, June 5. She also commended staff for their work on the Service Centre open house on Saturday, June 6. Despite the weather, everyone seemed to have a good time.

Councillor Vasic wanted to highlight that the Croyden-Southwick Neighbourhood BBQ was on Saturday, June 6, marking its 32nd year. She was not able to make it, but it was a beautiful celebration that brings together the neighbours, which the Neighbourhoods Team enables.
Councillor Vasic also mentioned the Lincoln Heights Garage Sale is this coming Saturday, June 13 from 8am-12pm.
Councillor Wright wanted to echo how great it is to have the ongoing Service Centre open house. It was great to make connections, and even bump into residents from Ward 7.

Councillor Wright also highlighted that the Uptown Square has had a lot of activities happening all the time. In addition to the Pride and Indigenous History Month kickoff, Trillium Lutheran Church has painted their stairway at the front of the church down to the street with a rainbow. It’s very bright and colourful, and a great spot to do photos.

They were also host to a performance as part of the Open Ears festival this past weekend, on Saturday, June 6. The Open Ears festival has been going on for years across Kitchener and Waterloo, and showcases modern musical composition.
